appraisal_events.evidence: The departing guests form «un long défilé, mais un défilé devant le baron seul» — «Personne n'eût plus pensé à se faire présenter à Mme Verdurin qu'à l'ouvreuse d'un théâtre» — several pretend not to recognize her and take their leave of another guest's wife instead, and Mme d'Arpajon asks within her hearing «Est-ce qu'il y a seulement jamais eu un M. Verdurin ?»; meanwhile duchesses queue to thank «Palamède qui s'est donné tant de peine», «Il n'y a que lui qui puisse à l'heure actuelle donner des fêtes pareilles», several engage Charlie on the spot for their own evenings, and even M. d'Argencourt, once so hard on men of the baron's kind, is «aussi aimable et flagorneur» and asks to be introduced to Morel.
appraisal_events.explanation: In her own salon the hostess is erased and the whole homage is transferred to Charlus, who is publicly crowned as the only man in Paris able to give such a party, with Morel booked on the strength of it.

appraisal_events.evidence: «Hé bien, êtes-vous contente ?... le poids que j'ai soulevé, le volume d'air que j'ai déplacé pour vous. Vous avez eu la reine de Naples...» ; her own share is that of «le page qui arma Jeanne d'Arc», she is congratulated for having had «le bon esprit» to ask him to guarantee the evening's prestige, lectured on why «Vous auriez invité la Molé que tout était raté» — «C'est une sotte, ne l'invitez plus» — and finally told that Mme de Duras has engaged Morel and that he thinks of asking an invitation «pour M. Verdurin», which the narration calls «le plus sanglant outrage pour l'épouse».
appraisal_events.explanation: The baron converts her party into his own achievement to her face and closes by arranging a sequel from which she alone is left out, while disposing of her guest list; his own condescension, not merely the guests' rudeness, does the cutting.

appraisal_events.evidence: He is «porté sur un nuage» and cannot see her fury; his eloquence, genuine, is fed only «des thèmes insignifiants» by «ses colères de vieille femme et sa culture de mondain»; his verdicts on society women are said to be inflated «follement» by rancour, since «le monde étant le royaume du néant»; and his final boast is delivered «emporté par la démence de ceux que Jupiter veut perdre».
appraisal_events.explanation: At the very summit of his triumph the narration hollows it out, rating both the world he rules and his judgment of it at nothing and announcing the ruin his blindness is preparing.

appraisal_events.evidence: He flatly contradicts her musical taste («Oui, c'est une horreur»), corrects her «votre ami» into «mon protégé» «sans plus de pitié pour le savoir grammatical que pour les dons musicaux de sa cousine», answers her whispered proposal «d'une voix forte et capable d'être entendue de tout le salon», refuses her offer of help, and dismisses her «non en lui disant au revoir, mais en se tournant vers la personne qui venait immédiatement après»; her plotting glance meanwhile tells Mme de Valcourt «Marie-Thérèse arrange avec Palamède quelque chose dont je ne dois pas faire partie», and the narration says the sorting of guests «ravale si bas» the women who practise it.
appraisal_events.explanation: The cousin who came for a piece of his prestige is publicly corrected, exposed and shown the door, and her attempt to keep her exclusion of Mme de Valcourt secret betrays it instead.

status_effects.explanation: Deference is withheld from her in her own house before the whole room: unrecognized, unpresented to, compared to a theatre usherette, and doubted to exist at all.
The evening's whole homage converges on him; duchesses wait in line to thank him and even an old enemy of his kind now flatters him.
Called a violinist of genius, engaged on the spot by several great ladies and sought out for introductions, he gains standing that the evening visibly confers.
A boundary closes on her: her own violinist is engaged for Mme de Duras's evening and the invitation the baron proposes to obtain is for her husband alone.

Charlus makes her the one guest whose presence would have wrecked everything and orders her dropped, and the narration seconds him to the extent of saying she was never equal to her reputation for intelligence.
The narration's verdict runs against the room's: his triumph is the delusion of a man the gods have decided to destroy, his eloquence wasted on nothing.
Every move she makes misfires: her compliment is called a horror, her phrasing corrected, her whisper broadcast, her offer of help refused.
The dismissal is witnessed: he ends the audience like a doctor closing a consultation, turning to the next person without saying good night to her.
She is designated «l'exclue» of the projected evening and reads her exclusion in the glance meant to conceal it, though the party in question will never take place.

ambiguities: The passage runs two opposed verdicts on Charlus at once: the assembled world crowns him as the evening's only author, while the narration rates his empire and his judgments at nothing and calls his triumph the madness that precedes ruin.
